regions.power_system: Saint Helena operates a diesel-dependent isolated power system operated by Connect St Helena Ltd, with no grid interconnection to any other territory or mainland. The island's electricity is generated by diesel gensets; the territory has been seeking to reduce diesel dependency through renewable energy projects.
regions.price: £0.40/unit for Domestic Band 1 (first 1,000 units) and £0.61/unit for Domestic Band 2 (units over 1,000) and Commercial, effective 1st July 2024 through 30th June 2025
regions.nuclear_position: Saint Helena is declared a nuclear-free zone by statute. No nuclear weapons, facilities, or equipment for nuclear weapons production, storage, processing or disposal are permitted, with exceptions only for radioactive materials for medical purposes.
regions.microreactor_activity: PASH (Paving the way for Alternative Sources of Energy in Saint Helena) project selected as preferred bidder to provide renewable energy solution to reduce diesel dependence; no nuclear-specific studies or reactor interest found.
blockers: Saint Helena's nuclear-free zone declaration prohibits civil nuclear power without legislative change
Island population (~4,200) is sub-1 MW per capita load, well below any current microreactor minimum size
PASH renewable project is the incumbent solution for reducing diesel dependency
regions.microreactor_read: Saint Helena's nuclear-free zone ban and sub-4 MW island load both preclude near-term microreactor deployment; a reactor would require legislative carve-out for civil power (distinct from existing weapons ban), making it a multi-decade political process.

regions.claim: On April 22, 2026, the Government of Yukon signed a formal partnership agreement with the Government of Ontario 'to strengthen collaboration on energy development, with a focus on improving long-term reliability and exploring emerging technologies such as small modular reactors.'
regions.evidence: Partnership agreement signed April 22, 2026 (confirmed as April 22 in primary release); Ontario Power Generation and Yukon Energy are collaborating on necessary groundwork for SMR deployment; the agreement includes exploration of microreactors for off-grid applications in remote communities and mines.
